text:
anya: heads-up — seeing a p95 jump in per-token latency on /chat-stream around 14:02 UTC. token_ttft up ~60ms vs last baseline :eyes:
kevin: saw the alert, alertbot fired for route_slo_deviation. link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/g/rtoken (will paste panels) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
alertbot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /chat-stream — p95_token_latency=480ms (threshold=400ms)
mauro: quick glance from perf nodes: decode_post looks stable, but kernel_exec shows intermittent spikes. some hosts are using int8-runner variant more often than baseline
sophie: do we have kv cache hit-rate data? a KV miss would push more work into kernel + prefix fetch and spike TTFT
kevin: running a quick prom query now, past 10m:
```promql
sum by (kernel_variant) (rate(kernel_exec_ms_sum[5m])) / sum by (kernel_variant) (rate(kernel_exec_ms_count[5m]))
```
anya: pulled a handful of traces. span order per token: network -> prequeue -> batch_wait -> kvcache_lookup -> kernel_execute -> decode_post. majority of delta is prequeue + kvcache_lookup in the bad windows
mauro: can you paste p50/p95 for spans? also what fraction of requests hit optimized kernels vs fallbacks?
anya: sample (p50 / p95 ms): prequeue 5 / 18, batch_wait 2 / 9, kvcache_lookup 8 / 120, kernel_execute 12 / 30, decode_post 3 / 8. kv hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~63% across the pool during spike
sophie: that kv miss spike coincides with an infra change to eviction policy yesterday. @kevin did we flip any TTLs / eviction rules?
kevin: yep, we rolled PR #789 at 02:30 UTC that tightened large-key TTLs to reduce memory pressure. rolling it back now after seeing this correlation
deploy-bot: rollback PR #789 initiated — target pool: g4dn-pool-17 (rolling update)
anya: while rollback runs, proposal for short-term telemetry improvements: 1) attach `kernel_variant` tag to token-level metrics (token_ttft_ms, token_kernel_ms), 2) emit `kv_lookup_result` (hit|miss|stale) per token, 3) sample 1/1000 tokens with full span traces (for trace viewer)
mauro: +1. also want a kernel-attribution panel: aggregated kernel_exec_ms by kernel_variant + quantization level, and a stacked waterfall that composes token_ttft from spans so we can visually attribute regressions
kevin: I'll open a dashboard patch and a quick RFC. will also temporarily relax the alert thresholds while rollback is in flight :sweat_smile:
sophie: add a route-level KPI for kv_hit_ratio and a short runbook note that TTL/eviction changes must be coordinated with runtime folks. we had no explicit owner on that config change
anya: dashboard patch notes: add `token_ttft_without_network = token_ttft_ms - network_ms` derived metric; add sampled traces panel with link to trace viewer; add `kernel_variant` legend and a table of recent kernel switches per-host
kevin: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/ops/telemetry/pulls/1245 — prom rules + grafana panels. pinging @oncall for incident monitoring
oncall: paging kevin for SLO incident (assigned)
oncall: I'll watch the pools. if rollback finishes and kv hit-rate recovers we'll close the incident
deploy-bot: rollback complete on g4dn-pool-17 at 14:12 UTC, traffic shifted back to baseline hosts
anya: post-rollback quick check: kv hit-rate back to ~90% within 2 minutes, p95 token latency dropped to ~360ms. Looks like eviction TTL was the culprit.
mauro: great. next steps: merge telemetry PR, add kernel_variant tagging at runtime, and add automated alert that correlates sudden kv_hit drops with p95 token increases
kevin: filing follow-up RFC for kernel tagging + sampling plan. I'll schedule a short sync with infra and runtime to avoid TTL surprises. thanks all :thumbsup:
anya: closing here but will leave the dashboard PR open for review and will record the incident in our postmortem tracker
__notes: This thread is a single Slack conversation string with messages prefixed by sender names as required by agents.md. Timestamps are plausible and metadata fields are strings or lists of strings.
